questions.question:
Three statements are followed by three conclusions numbered I, II, III. You have to consider these statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts. Decide which of the given conclusions logically follows from the given statements.

**Statements :**

No Mango is a banana.

No banana is a guava.

Some guavas are oranges.

**Conclusions :**

(I) Some mangoes are oranges.

(II) Some guavas are mangoes.

(III) No orange is a banana.

options.text: Conclusions I, II and III follow.

questions.solution:
From the given statements, the Venn diagram is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1eea165fa8f5dae77d8bd91c2527fce431f604a5dc59e4d9ad5b0b881a00a0b1.png] 

Now we consider the given conclusions:

(I) Some mangoes are oranges → Does not follow → We have no information about the relation between mangoes and oranges and we cannot assume anything, so the conclusion does not follow.

(II) Some guavas are mangoes** **→ Does not follow → We have no information about the relation between mangoes and guavas and we cannot assume anything, so the conclusion does not follow.

(III) No orange is a banana** **→ Does not follow → As some oranges are guavas but there is no evidence about the rest of the oranges so we cannot relate anything on our own and thus the conclusion does not follow.

So, none of the conclusion follow.

Hence **the correct answer is option 2)**

questions.question:
Two different position of the same dice are shown, having letters H, I, J, K, L and M written on its faces are shown.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9c852c5f9214373e6314d1c997c7d0e6331fbf5bf1dd4dc5f9aeb64a43cb88ec.png] 

Which letter is on the face opposite to the face having H on it?
questions.solution:
When we observe both the figures we see:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c16a6770362d9b21fd7c70dd46fb584ebb664edcba1da3d2dce2e7ae792fea1d.png] 

The dice is turned having L on the same positions which means H, I, J, K are the four sides of the dice.

L →L

J → K

H → I

Now when the dice is rotated H comes at the place of I and J comes at the place of K which means **H is opposite to I.**

Hence **the correct answer is option 2)**

Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set.

(NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 - Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is NOT allowed)

(9, 4, 85)

(6, 5, 41)
questions.solution:
The pattern followed in the given sets is:**
 **(**First term)² + Second term = Third term**

We apply the pattern on the given sets:

1) (9, 4, 85)

(9)² + 4 = 85 

81 + 4 = 85

85 = 85

2) (6, 5, 41)

(6)2 + 5 = 41 

36 + 5 = 41

41 = 41

Now we apply the pattern on the given options:

Option 1) (8, 2, 228)

(8)2 + 2 = 228 
64 + 2 = 228
66 ≠ 228

Option 2) (2, 15, 39)

(2)2 + 15 = 39 
4 + 15 = 39
19 ≠ 39

Option 3) (3, 9, 19)

(3)2 + 9 = 19 
9 + 9 = 19
18 ≠ 19

Option 4) (1, 4, 5)

(1)2 + 4 = 5 
1 + 4 = 5
5 = 5

Hence **the correct answer is option 4)**

questions.question:
Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements :**

Some C are P.

No C is a T.

All P are S.

**Conclusions :**

I. All S being C is a possibility.

II. At least some T are not C.

III. Some P are not T's.

options.text: Only conclusions II and III follow
All conclusions I, II and III follow
Only conclusions I and III follow

questions.solution:
From the statements, the Venn diagram is:

Some C are P.

No C is a T.

All P are S.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3289932017d92efbe1aedde0496c687ed5849f6ec5ebf676644baefe8048fd3a.png] 

Now we consider the given conclusions:

I. All S being C is a possibility → Follow [ As some C are P then there is a possibility that all S are C to be true and therefore the conclusion follows.] 

II. At least some T are not C → Follow [As no C is a T, So, itis definitely true some T are not C]

III. Some P are not T's** **→ Follow →[The common part of C and P will not T, So it is definitely true.]

So all the conclusions follow.

Hence **the correct answer is option 3)**
